We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x$ and $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sin⁡x)=cos⁡x.$ Applying these formulas, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x+2sin⁡x) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡x+2cos⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(0)+2cos⁡(0) \\  & =1+2(1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope is $3.$
